modality_preference.survey_note: REACH MSNA, 20 Sep-15 Oct 2025, face-to-face; factsheet gives n=6,988 in one place and 6,326 in another. Question wording not in the factsheet. Earlier MSNA 2024 (n=12,233) ranked in-kind food 68%, mobile-money cash 38%, physical cash 33%. HNRP 2026 p.14 (qualitative): consultations by GTS, Loop and the CEA Taskforce confirm cash remains the preferred modality, particularly for women-, older-person- and child-headed households, persons with disabilities and IDPs. No figure in the plan.

ai_summary.headline: Somalia has made MPCA the first-line modality on paper, but only about a third of the USD 97M is funded.
ai_summary.narrative: Cash is unusually prominent in the 2026 plan. MPC is a dedicated USD 97M line (11.4% of the USD 852M appeal) and, per the gDCF reading of the HNRP, total CVA is USD 365.5M, 43% of requirements [s1][s5]. The Humanitarian Coordinator calls MPCA the first-line response modality and the CWG issued a framework in February 2026 making it the default for households with multiple needs [s2][s11]. Funding does not yet match the ambition: the plan is 35.5% funded and MPC has received USD 35.1M, 36.2% of its line [s1]. The pooled fund shows no MPC-tagged projects in 2025 or 2026, so MPC relies on bilateral donors [s6]. Household preference looks split rather than cash-dominant: 78% named cash and 78% in-kind in the 2025 MSNA [s7]. Market monitoring appears to be in place through FSNAU/FEWS NET [s12]. The CWG is co-led by WFP and Concern with an OCHA co-chair role [s9][s14]; no cash feasibility study was found.
barriers: MPC funding is 36% of its line, so the first-line modality may not be deliverable at scale
Pooled fund allocations carry no MPC cluster tag
Cash and in-kind are tied in stated preference, which supports mixed responses
Cluster sections of the HNRP are reported to vary in CVA depth [s5]
opportunities: HC-level endorsement of MPCA gives CALP a clear advocacy hook for pooled-fund and bilateral funding
MPCA exit pathway to the Baxnaano safety net links humanitarian cash to national systems [s5]
data_gaps: sectoral cash share of funding and pooled funds

total_funding_usd.note: All incoming funding to the plan, pledges excluded. Matches the FTS plan summary.

mpc_usd.note: FTS single-cluster view of the Multi Purpose Cash cluster; shared-cluster view US$35.1M. Incoming flows, pledges excluded.

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 36 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Refugee Response US$13.2M, Food Security and Livelihoods US$7.1M, Protection US$6.3M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

cva_pct_of_total.note: cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

sectoral_cva_pct_of_total.note: sectoral_cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

mpc_pct_of_total.note: MPC cluster funding as a share of total plan funding (single-cluster view).

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.

localisation.framework: IASC MPC scaling plan, objective 4 (local leadership and co-implementation)

cva_to_local_pct.note: Indicator 4.2 proxy. Share of FTS cash funding (MPC cluster or CTP tag, US$62.4M) whose first-level recipient is a local or national NGO/CSO or a national government body. FTS does not see sub-grants, so this understates money that reaches local actors through international intermediaries.

all_funding_to_local_pct.note: Share of all plan funding whose first-level recipient is a local or national actor (US$2.8M). Same first-level caveat.

cbpf_cva_to_local_pct.note: Second-level view: share of the pooled fund's cash grants (US$2.4M) that went to local or national actors. Pooled-fund grants are the one onward layer FTS records.

cbpf_all_to_local_pct.note: Share of all pooled-fund grants inside the plan (US$23.0M) to local or national actors.

localisation.caveat: FTS sees first-level recipients only; indicator 4.2 as defined (direct donor allocation to local partners) is therefore a floor. Chair roles come from public CWG pages and may be out of date.
